A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same AMD study, with complete main text and Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of the equations, tables, figures and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original AMD image/video benchmark results, component ablations, training analyses and 2D simulations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, training analyses and simulations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: Dynamic Score Adaptation, reward-based group advantages and Repulsive Landscape Sharpening in Sections 3.2–3.3 are unchanged, as is Algorithm 1 in Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-generation, streaming-video, image-to-video and 2D toy scenarios. Appendix F retains the same supplementary benchmarks, including the internal image-to-video benchmark.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the reported experiments. LongLive already appears in v1's Table 6; naming it in the expanded caption introduces no new comparison.

E3.justification: Metrics, sample sizes, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The streaming-video task and Wan-1.3B backbone named in the new Table 6 caption were already specified in Section 4.2 and Appendix A.4.

E4.justification: The component ablations, training-dynamics analysis, reward-landscape experiments and naive-adaptation comparison in Section 4.3 and Appendix F.1 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged. Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative samples are unchanged. For example, Table 6 retains VBench totals of 173.59 for LongLive and 197.45 for AMD; Appendix F's supplementary results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and propositions in Section 3, together with the proofs and derivations in Appendix C, are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same Forbidden Zone diagnosis, unified optimization perspective, AMD contributions and performance claims.

C2.justification: The expanded Table 6 caption repeats the existing interpretation of visual and motion quality gains. The text-alignment trade-off discussed in Section 4.2 and the reward-proxy limitations in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A's implementation, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures and Appendix F.2's benchmark-release plan are unchanged. The new caption repeats previously disclosed setup information.

R1.justification: The bibliography, Appendix B's related-work discussion and Section 3.1's positioning relative to other DMD methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 completes Table 6's placeholder caption, adds an explicit equal-contribution footnote and updates the version/date text. The remaining prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 6's expanded caption causes minor reflow on pages 7–9, including shifts in Figures 4 and 6 and the conclusion. No figures or tables are added or removed, and their underlying displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 replaces Table 6's unfinished 'Quantitative comparison...' caption with useful task, backbone, comparator and metric context, improving its standalone readability. The equal-contribution note also clarifies the existing author asterisks. These are limited editorial gains; the scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged.
